* ☁️ Add FastAPI Cloud deployment. PR [#2438](https://github.com/fastapi/full-stack-fastapi-template/pull/2438) by [@tiangolo](https://github.com/tiangolo).

### Internal

* 👷 Migrate automatic labels to Latest Changes. PR [#2439](https://github.com/fastapi/full-stack-fastapi-template/pull/
* ♻️ Migrate to `DATABASE_URL` instead of separate variables. PR [#2184](https://github.com/fastapi/full-stack-fastapi-template/pull/2184) by [@patrick91](https://github.com/patrick91).

* 🔧 Refactor PostgreSQL env var config. PR [#2392](https://github.com/fastapi/full-stack-fastapi-template/pull/2392) by [@tiangolo](https://github.com/tiangolo).

**Upgrading.** A production stack takes the new network range by being taken down and up once: `git pull`, then `sudo docker compose -p noctornal-prod -f infra/production/compose.yml down`, then the same with `up -d --build`. The console is down for about twenty seconds and the data volumes are kept. Do not skip the `down`: a plain `up -d --build` leaves the stack half started. **The installer no longer races Postgres's first start.** Installing the published Alpha 7 zip on a clean machine (a fresh Ubuntu 24.04 VM) for the first time found that, on a fresh volume, the installer's readiness probe answered on the Unix socket of the Postgres image's temporary init server, so the installer ran the migrations into "the database system is starting up" and stopped. The probe now goes over TCP, where only the real server answers, as the compose healthcheck does. A test holds it. Only a fi

**Upgrading is not a drop-in.** Read [Upgrading from Alpha 6](https://github.com/dboudreau00/NocTORnal/blob/v0.7.0-alpha/release/CHANGELOG.md#upgrading-from-alpha-6) first. Alpha 6 stands at Alembic 0068, so the upgrade applies 56 revisions, 0069 to 0124; several change existing data and many refuse a downgrade once the new features hold data. In short:
**Every way out goes through one door.** Every outbound connection the product makes now goes through one pinned client, one address policy and one function

**Security work.** Collection fetches are protected against DNS rebinding: each hop is resolved once, checked, and connected to by number, with the certificate still checked against the name, and each fetch has a wall-clock allowance, so a source that answers one byte at a time can no longer hold the collector. A production process refuses to start on any credential this repository or MinIO publishes.
